title: Defence Legislation Amendment (Superannuation and ADF Cover) Bill 2015
short_title: Defence Legislation Amendment (Superannuation and ADF Cover) Bill 2015

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: This bill is part of a three-bill package that creates a new superannuation scheme for Australian Defence Force members and supports a new workforce model.

The package includes the Australian Defence Force Superannuation Bill 2015, which lets new ADF members from 1 July 2016 choose their superannuation scheme and transfer benefits when leaving, and the Australian Defence Force Cover Bill 2015, which provides separate death and invalidity cover.
The package also includes draft trust deeds and an instrument that makes consequential changes to the Military Superannuation and Benefits Scheme Trust Deed and Rules to reduce red tape.
changes: Establishes the Australian Defence Force Superannuation Scheme (ADF Super).
Introduces standalone statutory death and invalidity cover under ADF Cover.
Makes administrative changes to the MSBS Trust Deed and Rules to reduce red tape.
summary.affected: Permanent members of the Australian Defence Force (ADF) and people joining the ADF on and after 1 July 2016.

speeches.speaker: Stuart Robert
speeches.brief: The bill establishes ADF Super and ADF Cover, raises the age for children to prove full-time education from 16 to 18, allows re-entered members to choose their super fund while continuing to receive retirement pay, and introduces flexible service arrangements for permanent ADF members.

speeches.speaker: David Feeney
speeches.brief: The speaker supported the ADF Superannuation bills, which create a new super scheme with greater flexibility and portability, and noted that after Labor's opposition, a single employer contribution rate of 16.4% replaced the proposed two-tiered system.

speeches.speaker: Ewen Jones
speeches.brief: The speaker announced that the Australian Defence Force Superannuation Bill 2015 and related bills will introduce ADF Super from 1 July 2016, giving members a 16.4% contribution rate and the ability to choose their superannuation fund, along with ADF Cover for death and invalidity and new part-time work options; the existing Military Superannuation and Benefits Scheme will close to new members from that date.

speeches.speaker: Graham Perrett
speeches.brief: Labor supported the Australian Defence Force Superannuation Bill 2015, the Australian Defence Force Cover Bill 2015, and the Defence Legislation Amendment (Superannuation and ADF Cover) Bill 2015, which establish the ADF Super scheme and standalone ADF Cover from 1 July 2016. The party endorsed the single 16.4% employer contribution rate, rejecting the government's original two-tier proposal, and argued the new scheme's flexibility would aid recruitment, particularly for women.

speeches.speaker: John Alexander
speeches.brief: The Abbott government introduced three bills to establish ADF Super, a new military superannuation scheme with a 16.4% employer contribution rate, ADF Cover for death and invalidity benefits, and part-time work options for full-time ADF members, effective from 1 July 2016. The reforms aim to improve flexibility and portability of superannuation, with 80% of personnel serving less than 15 years expected to benefit.

speeches.speaker: Craig Kelly
speeches.brief: The speaker announced the establishment of ADF Super, a new military superannuation scheme with a 16.4% employer contribution rate and member choice of fund, along with the ADF Cover death and invalidity scheme funded from consolidated revenue. He also argued in favour of allowing young Australians to access their superannuation for a first home deposit.
